_note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Berger Paints India (consolidated, ₹ crore). Berger reports one segment ('Paints and Coatings'), so the engine runs on a single revenue-growth path and an EBITDA-margin path; the business-line build (decorative vs industrial, sized on the company's FY26 split of 82% / 18%) sits in `businessLines` and the authoring script checks that it sums to model revenue. Other income = treasury yield × opening net cash (Screener basis) + non-treasury income (share of profit of the two 49% JVs plus income the Screener cash line does not explain). Valued on P/E, as the street does.
_revenueWhy: FY27 +12%: Q1 +12.0% (standalone volume +8.4%, price/mix ~5%; decorative value ~13.5%). Management guides to double-digit growth, Q2 'slightly ahead' of Q1 (volume 7.5-8%, price 7.5-8.5%) as industrial price rises flow in. H2 still carries the Mar-Jun 2026 price rises but faces possible post-Diwali cuts if crude stays lower (Brent fell ~15% in June) and bigger dealer rebates; we assume H2 ~+11%. FY28 +9%: price laps and part is given back; volume ~9% (FY26 standalone quarters ran 6-12%). FY29 +10%: volume ~9% plus ~1% mix. Business lines: decorative +12.5% / +9% / +10%, industrial +10% / +9% / +10%.

businessLines._why: Company split: industrial 18% of consolidated sales in FY26 (AR FY26 MD message), decorative the rest (~80% per CRISIL). Subsidiaries (Bolix, STP, Nepal) are inside these shares as the company reports them. FY27 decorative +12.5%: Q1 value ~13.5% and Q2 price impact 7.5-8.5% on ~8% volume, H2 slower. Industrial +10%: price rises came late in Q1 ('protracted battle'), catch up from Q2; protective helped by government capex; automotive by GST cuts.

_marginWhy: Consolidated EBITDA margin 16.1% (FY25), 15.4% (FY26), 16.9% in Q1FY27 (16.5% a year earlier). Guided range 15-17% (management, every quarter); CRISIL expects 15-17%. FY27 16.0%: Q2 is seasonally weak (12.5% in Q2FY26) but should be up year on year as industrial price rises flow in; H2 risks are dealer rebates and price give-backs. FY28 16.0%, FY29 16.2%: cheaper inputs offset by price give-backs and competitive spends; the new plants add fixed cost before they fill. Each 1pp of margin is ~₹145 cr of EBITDA (~7% of FY28E EPS).
_capexWhy: FY27 guidance ₹600-800 cr (5-Aug-2026); Panagarh (West Bengal) and Khordha (Odisha) plants cost ₹1,800-2,000 cr together, Panagarh to start at the end of FY27; CRISIL (28-Aug-2026) expects ~₹1,000 cr a year over the next few years. FY24-26 capex ₹275 / 429 / 518 cr (Screener).
_depWhy: FY26 depreciation ₹392 cr = 7.5% of average gross block (₹5,251 cr); Q1FY27 ₹103 cr (₹412 cr annualised). The engine depreciates capex at once while the new plants sit in CWIP until commissioned, so we use 7.0%: FY27E ≈ ₹410 cr, in line with the Q1 run-rate, rising as the plants start.
_treasuryWhy: 7% on opening net cash on Screener's basis (cash + investments - borrowings: Rs 859 cr at Mar-26), i.e. ~Rs 60 cr in FY27E, close to FY26 treasury income of Rs 61.8 cr (bank-deposit interest Rs 17.8 cr + mutual-fund gains Rs 44.0 cr, AR FY26 note 36). The company reports higher net cash (Rs 1,198 cr at Mar-26, Rs 1,424 cr at Jun-26): cash Rs 305 cr plus liquid mutual funds Rs 954 cr (AR note 54) less a little bank debt, whereas Screener deducts all borrowings including lease liabilities and adds the equity-accounted JV stakes. Using the company figure would add ~Rs 24 cr of income in FY27E (~1% of EPS); we stay on the Screener basis, which the model balance sheet uses.
_otherIncomeWhy: Non-treasury other income, built only from sourced parts. (1) Share of profit of the two 49% JVs (Berger Nippon Paint Automotive, Berger Becker): Rs 35 cr (FY25), Rs 51 cr (FY26, +46%), Rs 11.8 cr in Q1FY27 (+5%); management says both JVs grew strongly and passenger-car demand is buoyant after the GST cut, so we take Rs 55 / 60 / 65 cr (~8% a year, in line with industrial revenue). (2) Recurring non-treasury items in consolidated other income (AR FY26 note 36): interest on non-bank items Rs 4.2 cr, discount income Rs 7.2 cr, arrangement fees Rs 1.8 cr, gains on early lease terminations Rs 5.4 cr and miscellaneous income Rs 15.0 cr = Rs 33.5 cr in FY26 (Rs 30.4 cr in FY25); held at Rs 33 cr. One-offs (insurance claims, gains on asset sales, balances written back, the FY25 fair-value gain on Surefire: Rs 11.4 cr in FY26, Rs 21.3 cr in FY25) are left out. FY27E total other income (incl. treasury) ~Rs 148 cr vs Rs 152 cr in the twelve months to Jun-26 on Screener (which also nets the Labour Code charge and the insurance recovery).
_interestWhy: FY26 ₹58 cr, Q1FY27 ₹12.5 cr; no long-term debt; plants funded from cash (CRISIL).
_taxWhy: FY26 ₹360 cr on ₹1,488 cr PBT (24.2%); Q1FY27 25.4% (₹137.6 cr on ₹542.6 cr). The engine taxes JV income (already post-tax) too, so 25% slightly understates EPS (~₹15 cr).
_payoutWhy: FY26 dividend ₹4.00 a share (₹466 cr, 41% of profit); FY25 ₹3.50 (35%). No buyback planned (MD, Feb-2026); capex absorbs cash.

dcf._betaWhy: Net cash, consumer-facing franchise with a dominant domestic business; below-market sensitivity (Ke 11.3%), same as the house treatment of Pidilite and Asian Paints-type compounders.
dcf._tgWhy: India's nominal GDP grows ~10%; per-capita paint use is 4.1 kg vs 13-15 kg globally, so the category can grow above GDP for long, but with more competitors. Top of the house 5-6% range: 6%.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~10% to 8% by year 15: volume growth of 8-10% a year has been steady, pricing is no longer a lever with Birla Opus and JSW in the market.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: Holds at 16%, the middle of management's 15-17% range.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex falls from ~5.6% of revenue (plant build) to 3.5%, near the FY24-26 average of ~3.7%.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Price rises stick through FY28 while inputs ease, Birla Opus and JSW Dulux stay rational (Investec's 'peak intensity is over'), volume runs at 10-11% on new stores and tinting machines, and margin sits at the top of the 15-17% range.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Prices are cut after Diwali faster than inputs fall, the challengers step up dealer schemes again and Berger loses share (as in 9MFY26), volume slows to 5-6% and margin drops to the bottom of the range.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Berger: P/E on FY28E or Jun-28E EPS (Nomura 50x FY28E, Monarch Networth 48x FY28E, Equirus 46x Jun-28E; ICICI Securities' DCF target equals ~40x FY28E). 37x = Berger's 52x median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021 (no trough years excluded: forward EPS never fell below half its prior three-year peak), cut by the ~30% median de-rating of four paint and adhesive peers (Asian Paints, Kansai Nerolac, Pidilite, Indigo) versus their five-year median P/E by 30-Sep-2026 (36.6x, rounded). No further growth adjustment: our FY27-29E EPS growth (~10% a year after the price-led FY27 jump) is in line with FY21-26 (~9%). Bull 45x (its 25th-percentile forward P/E since 2021); bear 29x (the median cut by the worst peer de-rating, Kansai Nerolac's 44%: Berger priced as a share loser).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Counts net cash at face value. 20x Sep-28E EBITDA = Berger's 36x median trailing EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021, less the same ~30% sector de-rating (25.5x trailing), restated for Sep-28E EBITDA being ~28% above the twelve months to Jun-26 (≈20x). Bull 24x, bear 16x scale with the P/E multiples.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF, Ke 11.3%, terminal growth 6%, plus net cash.
